stories.headline: Hasan Piker lashes out at Republicans, calls them 'terrorists' in event with Ilhan Omar
stories.note: Omar sharing a stage with a streamer calling Republicans terrorists gives the GOP a ready-made example of Democratic extremism.
body: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., co-hosted a campaign event in Minnesota on Monday night, attacking the Trump administration and Democrats who work with it.

During a Q&A moderated by former Minneapolis mayoral candidate Omar Fateh, Piker labeled Republicans "terrorists," while Omar called the GOP the "pedophile protection party" and predicted Trump would lose Minnesota a fourth time.
Piker also turned on moderate Democrats, saying the party gave ground to Trump in 2024 by treating migrants as a security threat, and calling any Democrat who won't reject that view "un-American."

The streamer had mostly been kept at arm's length by Democratic campaigns after a rough appearance with Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed last month, where his past claim that America "deserved" 9/11 resurfaced. El-Sayed later distanced himself, saying nobody speaks for his campaign but him and his staff.

Why it matters: A sitting congresswoman campaigning beside a commentator who calls Republicans terrorists hands the GOP a vivid example of how far the Democratic left has drifted, right before the midterms.

stories.headline: 'Dark money' group accused of 'scheme' to tip election in favor of Democrats, manipulate GOP voters
stories.note: Allegations of a hidden effort to manipulate GOP voters put Democrats on defense over election tactics.
body: A new group called the American Forge Coalition, which bills itself as "anti-globalist" and pro-American, has been mailing voters in battleground House districts attacking Republicans as not conservative enough, according to a Fox News Digital investigation.

Its targets include Reps. Mike Lawler (N.Y.), Brian Fitzpatrick (Pa.), Derrick Van Orden (Wis.), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (Iowa) and Jen Kiggans (Va.), plus North Carolina challenger Laurie Buckhout. Mailers accused some of backing "mass amnesty" and others of being soft on abortion, claims Fox says stretch the truth.

Lawler's campaign called it "a shady Democrat dark money scheme" meant to keep Republicans home as early voting starts. Fitzpatrick's team said the same left-wing playbook tells Republicans they're too independent and Democrats they're not independent enough.

The group was formed in May 2026, is registered in Delaware as a 501(c)(4), and doesn't have to disclose donors. A campaign-finance reform advocate said it could be a liberal-funded group posing as conservative, though its backers remain unknown. Fox noted a 2024 precedent tied to a group linked to former Rep. Eric Swalwell.
Why it matters: If it holds up, a stealth effort to depress GOP turnout in swing seats gives Republicans a strong argument that Democrats preach about protecting democracy while playing dirty to win.

stories.headline: Obama cozies up to Dem Party's socialist wing as former president makes surprising midterm moves
stories.note: Obama embracing the socialist wing helps Republicans paint the whole party as moving far left.
body: Former President Barack Obama is lending his star power to some of the Democratic Party's most left-wing candidates as the midterms close in.

On Saturday he rallied in Michigan with Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, a Medicare for All backer, and he endorsed Florida Senate nominee Angie Nixon, a DSA member running on universal childcare, rent protections and higher taxes on billionaires. He has also campaigned with Texas Senate candidate James Talarico.

Defending the party against charges it has gone too far left, Obama asked, "What is so radical about wanting everybody to have health care?" Critics online quickly pointed back to his own Obamacare promises.

The moves come after a string of socialist primary wins this year in Colorado, Michigan and New York. Democratic strategists argue Obama is simply building a big-tent coalition, while President Trump, at a Kansas rally, called him "a rotten president."
Why it matters: With the party's most popular figure embracing its socialist wing, Republicans can more easily argue that the left is now the Democratic mainstream.

stories.headline: Billionaire with Epstein ties emerges as top Dem donor bankrolling ads weaponizing disgraced financier's files
stories.note: A top Democratic donor with Epstein ties funding Epstein-themed attack ads is an awkward hypocrisy story for Democrats.
body: LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, who has faced scrutiny over his past ties to Jeffrey Epstein, was among the biggest donors to House Majority PAC, according to FEC filings released last week.

The Democratic super PAC is now running Epstein-themed attack ads against Republicans, including $543,300 against Rep. Nick Begich in Alaska, plus spending in Iowa, Pennsylvania and Arizona House races. Filings don't show which donor money paid for which ads.

Records in the DOJ's Epstein files library show Hoffman exchanged gifts and emails with Epstein and visited his island and New York home. Hoffman has denied wrongdoing and said in 2019 he deeply regretted helping repair Epstein's reputation. Fox notes there is no allegation he took part in Epstein's crimes.

An RNC spokesperson said Democrats don't mind money in politics as long as it helps them, even from donors who kept up a relationship with Epstein after his conviction. Fox said it asked HMP whether it knew of Hoffman's history when it took the money.
Why it matters: Democrats attacking Republicans over Epstein while relying on a donor with Epstein ties is a ready-made hypocrisy charge in the final week.

stories.headline: James Comey faces new DOJ case over alleged national defense disclosure
stories.note: A new case against Comey keeps accountability for Trump's old adversaries in the headlines.
body: The Justice Department has filed a two-count criminal information against former FBI Director James Comey in federal court in Washington, D.C., alleging he shared national defense information with an unauthorized person and conspired to disclose it.
Prosecutors say the alleged disclosure happened on or about Oct. 5, 2016. The DOJ said the filing was made to stop the statute of limitations from running out while its investigation continues.

Comey's lawyers argue the case can't proceed without a grand jury indictment. Judge Trevor McFadden held a closed emergency hearing Oct. 9, agreed to unseal the case, and hasn't yet ruled on the motion to dismiss.

Comey denied wrongdoing on Instagram, calling the move an "appalling abuse of the Department of Justice" and saying he's still innocent. This is the DOJ's third attempt to prosecute him; an earlier case was dismissed and another over his "86 47" post is pending.
Why it matters: For Republicans who have long wanted accountability for the Russia-probe era, the new case keeps Comey's conduct in the spotlight.

stories.headline: DHS suspends visa-free travel program for Chinese nationals amid birth tourism, security concerns
stories.note: A tough move on birth tourism and security from China plays to the GOP's strength on borders.
body: The Trump administration is suspending a Biden-era program that let prescreened Chinese nationals visit the Northern Mariana Islands for up to 14 days without a visa.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's department cited risks of birth tourism, espionage near U.S. military sites, and illegal onward travel to nearby Guam. More than 3,000 Chinese nationals used the program in fiscal 2025, DHS said.

The suspension takes effect Oct. 30 at 2 p.m. EDT for new and already-approved travelers. Sens. Mike Lee, Rick Scott, John Cornyn and Bill Cassidy had urged the move in April, and Lee cheered it, writing, "America is not a nursery for the CCP to steal citizenship."
It's part of a wider crackdown: a State Department task force had revoked more than 750 visas tied to suspected birth tourism as of late August.
Why it matters: Closing a loophole Republicans flagged on China and birth tourism shows the administration acting on border and national-security promises.

stories.headline: Haley Stevens ripped by fellow Dems for refusing to explicitly back El-Sayed: 'Stay the f--- off television'
stories.note: Open Democratic infighting in Michigan's Senate race is good news for Republicans there.
body: Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., who narrowly lost Michigan's Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, is taking fire from progressives for not clearly endorsing him on CNN's "State of the Union."
Stevens said she's "on the team" and backing the Democratic ticket, but admitted she can't say she agrees with everything that's happened, and didn't explicitly name El-Sayed.

Indivisible leader Leah Greenberg told anyone who can't give the nominee a full endorsement to stay off television, using an expletive. Commentators Mehdi Hasan and Emma Vigeland also blasted Stevens, while strategist Lis Smith pushed back in her defense.
El-Sayed won the primary 48.5% to 47.5%. Stevens was the establishment pick backed by Chuck Schumer, while El-Sayed has support from Squad members like Rashida Tlaib and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
Why it matters: A week before Election Day, open feuding between Michigan Democrats' establishment and progressive wings is a gift to Republicans in a must-watch Senate race.
